title: Kung Pao Prawns
subtitle: Sichuan stir-fried prawns with peanuts and dried chillies
excerpt: The prawn version of the Sichuan classic: king prawns stir-fried at ferocious heat with dried chillies, Sichuan pepper, peanuts, and spring onion in a tangy, mildly sweet sauce with the characteristic mala numbing-hot finish.

recipe.sourceNotes: Kung Pao (Gong Bao) chicken is one of the most famous Sichuan dishes, named for Ding Baozhen (1820-1886), a Qing Dynasty official whose title was Gong Bao (Palace Guardian). The prawn version follows the same formula: the key flavour combination is the numbing heat of Sichuan pepper, the dry heat of sichuan chillies, the crunch of peanuts, and a sauce that combines sweet (sugar), sour (vinegar), and savoury (soy sauce) notes. The heat of the wok is essential: the ingredients must be stir-fried at the highest possible heat for the characteristic wok hei (breath of the wok) flavour. The dried chillies should be toasted until just darkened but not burnt.

content.text: The wok must be smoking before the prawns go in. Have the sauce pre-mixed in a bowl before you start; the cooking goes fast. Toast the dried chillies in the oil first until they darken slightly; this is where the characteristic deep, smoky-hot flavour comes from. Do not burn them or the dish will be bitter.

items.preparation: small dried Sichuan chillies; or dried bird's eye chillies
mixed with 1 tbsp water; to thicken the sauce

content.text: Mix the sauce ingredients (soy, vinegar, sugar, sesame oil, and cornflour slurry) in a small bowl. Set aside. Heat the oil in a wok over the highest heat until smoking. Add the dried chillies and Sichuan pepper. Fry for 15 to 20 seconds until the chillies darken.
Add the prawns in a single layer. Do not move for 30 seconds to allow them to char slightly. Toss vigorously. Add the garlic and ginger. Stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add the spring onion and peanuts. Stir-fry for 30 seconds. Pour in the sauce mixture. Toss for 30 seconds until the sauce thickens and coats the prawns. Serve immediately over steamed white rice.
